lines.text: Adam! Wake up! Today is the big day!
I'm up, I'm up!
Eat something. You can't graduate on an empty stomach!
Mom, I'm too nervous to eat.
Nervous? Four years of exams, and now you're nervous?
Good morning, everyone! How do I look?
Dad… is that your wedding suit?
Yes. It still fits. Almost.
It's perfect, dear. Now let's go. We can't be late.
It's eight thirty! We're going to be late!
We're not going to be late.
Dad is never late… except for every family event.
Very funny, Lina.
Adam! Over here!
Sami! You came!
Of course! Congratulations, man. You're a graduate now. Welcome to real life!
Real life? That sounds scary.
Don't worry. It's scary for everyone at the beginning.
And now… Adam Fares!
Go, Adam! Woohoo!
That's my son!
I'm so proud of you!
Congratulations, Adam! So, tell me, where are you working now?
Um… I'm still looking.
Still looking? My neighbor's son found a job before he graduated. In a bank! With a car!
Adam will find something great. Right, Adam?
Yes… of course.
A certificate on the wall… but no job.
"Jobs for fresh graduates"… Thousands of jobs, and they all say the same thing: "Excellent English required."
OK. Excellent English. Let's start.

questions.q: What is funny about Dad's suit?
questions.a: It is his wedding suit, and it is a little small now.

questions.q: What does Sami say to Adam at the university?
questions.a: He says, "Congratulations! You're a graduate now. Welcome to real life!"

questions.q: What does the uncle ask, and how does Adam feel?
questions.a: He asks, "Where are you working now?" Adam feels bad because he doesn't have a job.

questions.q: What do all the job ads say?
Has someone ever asked you a question that made you feel uncomfortable? What happened?
questions.a: Example: Yes. My aunt asked me about my exam results, and I felt uncomfortable.
